newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: International shipbuilders bid for $1 bln UAE deal. [CORRECTED 20:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: International shipbuilders bid for $1 bln UAE deal. [CORRECTED 20:40 GMT]

text.p: International shipbuilders have submitted bids to the United Arab Emirates to supply the Gulf Arab state with fast patrol boats in a deal potentially worth $1 billion, industry executives said on Monday.
"The companies have submitted bids to the customer for technical and financial evaluation," said one. "They are interested in up to six ocean-capable patrol boats."
He said the price tag would depend on several factors -- from politics to number of vessels -- but estimated it would be in the region of $1 billion.
An industry source said the bids would be given on Tuesday to senior UAE officials who make military procurement decisions.

Contenders for the contract include Britain's Vosper Thorneycroft Plc, France's DCNI, international arm of the state-owned naval shipyard Direction des Construction Navales (DCN), Dutch state-owned Shipyard Koninklijke Schelde Groep and Germany's Lurssen.
Two U.S. firms -- Newport News Shipbuilding (corrects to remove erroneous reference to Newport being owned by Tenneco) and Halter Marine -- are also competing.
One industry executive said Vosper Thorneycroft's sale of patrol boats to the UAE in the 1970s could give it an edge in the current competition.

But an industry source familiar with official thinking said Vosper would be in a stronger position than other companies only if the UAE was satisfied with the vessels it had previously purchased from the company.
Lurssen sold the UAE six Technical Naval Craft (TNC 45) in the early 1980s.

It was not clear when the UAE would decide on the fast patrol boats, but industry sources have said they expected Abu Dhabi to make an announcement during the IDEX arms show in the UAE capital on March 16-19.
Industry sources said the UAE was also seeking frigates, minesweepers and other ships as part of efforts to bolster naval defences against a potential threat from Iran across the Gulf.
Abu Dhabi and Tehran are locked in a dispute over three strategic Gulf islands located near key shipping lanes. Iran has angered the UAE by building up its presence on the islands.
"The fast patrol boats can be used both militarily and to fight drug smuggling and the illegal immigrants trying to enter the country," said an industry executive.
Abu Dhabi has emerged as a key customer in the international arms market. It spent about $6 billion in the 1987-94 period on arms imports and more deals are in the pipeline.
